title: CML Approval Endpoints: Molecular, Cytogenetic and Hematologic Responses Accepted by FDA and EMA
summary: Primary endpoints and pivotal trial designs (MMR, CCyR, MCyR and hematologic response) behind FDA and EMA approvals of chronic myeloid leukemia therapies.
body_markdown:
## CML approval endpoints: what FDA and EMA have accepted for MMR, CCyR, MCyR and hematologic response


Regulators have accepted chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) approvals on response endpoints or progression-free survival, not on overall survival. Which response they accept depends on three things: disease phase, line of therapy, and how much follow-up is available. Over the past two decades the accepted primary endpoint has moved from hematologic and cytogenetic response toward molecular response. The tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) approvals below show each step of that shift. FDA has usually granted accelerated approval on early response data and converted it to regular approval once longer follow-up confirmed durability. EMA's CHMP has generally accepted the same endpoints, with its own views on timepoints and comparators.


### Key takeaways


- **Newly diagnosed chronic phase (CP):** the primary endpoint moved from progression-free survival or time to progression (imatinib, December 2002) to major molecular response (MMR) at 12 months (nilotinib, June 2010) or confirmed complete cytogenetic response (CCyR) within 12 months (dasatinib, October 2010), then to MMR at 12 months (bosutinib) and MMR at 48 weeks (asciminib)[783](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=783)[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=128)[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=273)[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=627)[598](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=598) . Nilotinib's MMR-based first-line approval preceded dasatinib's CCyR-based approval. Every first-line approval in this group used a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial.
- **Resistant or intolerant CP:** major cytogenetic response (MCyR) from single-arm trials supported most approvals (imatinib after interferon, dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, omacetaxine)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=93)[278](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=278)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=133)[631](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=631)[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=384)[313](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=313) . Asciminib moved this setting to a randomized trial with MMR at 24 weeks as the primary endpoint[346](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=346)[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=603) .
- **Accelerated and blast phase:** major hematologic response (MaHR, defined as complete hematologic response plus no evidence of leukemia) has been the standard primary endpoint[278](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=278)[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=388)[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=319) . FDA removed "return to chronic phase" from the composite when it reviewed nilotinib[506](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=506)[507](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=507) .
- **Current guidance:** FDA guidance describes durable MMR as a surrogate endpoint used for traditional approval in CML[686](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=686) . EMA's 2016 haematological malignancies appendix recommends MMR at 18 months as the primary endpoint in superiority trials[760](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=760)[761](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=761) .


### Regulatory framework: FDA and EMA guidance


#### FDA


The 2020 final guidance *Hematologic Malignancies: Regulatory Considerations for Use of Minimal Residual Disease in Development of Drug and Biological Products for Treatment*[739](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=739) defines MMR as BCR-ABL(IS) below 0.1%. Where an RT-qPCR(IS) assay is not available, it defines MMR as a reduction of more than 3 logs in BCR-ABL1 mRNA from the standardized baseline[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=684) . The guidance says that achieving MMR predicts better long-term PFS/EFS and that "durable MMR can be a measure of clinical benefit"[685](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=685) . It calls for International Scale assays with the standardized baseline set at 100%, names RT-qPCR(IS) as the preferred method[791](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=791) , and notes that MRD can be used to select and monitor patients for TKI discontinuation[792](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=792) .


The FDA guidance *Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics* states that "durable major molecular response is a surrogate endpoint used for traditional approval for therapies in chronic myelogenous leukemia"[686](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=686) .


Product reviews show how FDA applies this in practice. In the asciminib first-line review, the Division described MMR with at least 12 months of follow-up as accepted for accelerated approval in newly diagnosed CP-CML, and MMR with at least five years of follow-up as a basis for regular approval[484](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=484) .


#### EMA


EMA's recommendations have changed across versions of the anticancer guideline:


Guideline version Recommended primary endpoint, CP-CML Notes


Draft, 19 November 2008 PFS preferred as the primary endpoint for non-inferiority trials Draft only[766](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=766)[767](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=767)


Appendix 2 (confirmatory studies in haematological malignancies), 3 March 2010 CCyR at one year for first-line superiority trials; at least 5 years of follow-up Molecular response accepted as a secondary endpoint only[765](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=765)


Appendix 4, Revision 2, 1 July 2016 MMR at 18 months for superiority trials against a licensed comparator; CCyR at 12 months, PFS and OS as secondary endpoints Other timepoints acceptable if justified; at least 8 years of follow-up expected; non-inferiority trials need MCyR assessed after at least two years[760](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=760)[761](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=761)


### Newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML


Product / trial Design and comparator Primary endpoint Result FDA pathway EMA/CHMP position


Imatinib, Study 0106 Randomized, open-label phase 3 vs interferon-alfa plus cytarabine, 553 per arm, crossover allowed[779](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=779)[780](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=780)[781](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=781)[782](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=782)[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=82) PFS, with progression including loss of CHR or MCyR; MCyR was the main endpoint for the first interim analysis[783](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=783)[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=78) 30-month PFS 87.8% vs 68.3% (p<0.0001)[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=86) Accelerated approval December 20, 2002; commitments fulfilled with long-term Study 0106 data in 2009[944](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=944)[947](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=947)[948](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=948) CPMP: CCyR not yet validated as a marker of clinical benefit, although an association could reasonably be assumed[546](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=546)


Dasatinib, DASISION Randomized, open-label vs imatinib 400 mg, n=519[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=273) Confirmed CCyR (two assessments at least 28 days apart) within 12 months[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=273) 76.8% vs 66.2% (P=0.007)[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=274) Accelerated approval October 28, 2010, with a 60-month follow-up requirement; regular approval August 12, 2015[908](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=908)[909](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=909)[910](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=910)[913](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=913) CHMP endorsed cCCyR at 12 months, considered CCyR validated, and said MMR could also have been acceptable[455](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=455)[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=456)


Nilotinib, ENESTnd (CAMN107A2303) Randomized 1:1:1, open-label phase 3 vs imatinib[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=55)[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=126) MMR (BCR-ABL ≤0.1% IS) at 12 months[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=128)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=56) 44% vs 22% (P<0.0001)[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=129) Accelerated approval June 17, 2010; Subpart H required a 24-month interim report and at least 60 months of follow-up, fulfilled in 2015[725](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=725)[726](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=726)[735](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=735)[736](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=736) CHMP accepted 12-month MMR as a surrogate primary endpoint when supported by secondary endpoints[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=63)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=64)


Bosutinib, BELA (3160A4-3000-WW) Randomized, open-label phase 3 vs imatinib[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=251)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=252) CCyR at one year[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=251) Primary objective failed[253](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=253)[575](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=575) Not approved on this trial; FDA did not allow secondary endpoints to be treated as primary after the primary failure[575](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=575)[576](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=576) CHMP: one-year CCyR acceptable as a primary objective for a superiority trial, not a non-inferiority trial[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=254)


Bosutinib, BFORE (AV001) Randomized 1:1, open-label vs imatinib[626](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=626)[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=237)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=238) MMR at 12 months[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=627)[239](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=239) 47% vs 37% (p=0.0200)[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=627)[628](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=628) Accelerated approval December 19, 2017, with a 60-month PMR; regular approval May 14, 2021[866](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=866)[867](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=867)[869](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=869)[870](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=870)[871](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=871)[872](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=872) CHMP accepted 12-month MMR as a surrogate and noted that updated guidance recommends superiority on MMR at 18 months[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=242)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=243)


Asciminib, ASC4FIRST Randomized 1:1, open-label vs investigator-selected TKI (imatinib, nilotinib, dasatinib or bosutinib)[597](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=597)[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=352)[353](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=353) MMR at week 48, overall and in the imatinib stratum[598](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=598)[354](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=354) 68% vs 49% overall; 69% vs 40% in the imatinib stratum[598](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=598)[599](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=599) Accelerated approval October 29, 2024; regular approval requires five years of efficacy follow-up[970](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=970)[971](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=971)[822](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=822) One pivotal study for the first-line extension; MMR at week 96 is the key secondary endpoint[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=352)[356](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=356)


Two design points come out of the first-line reviews:


- **Open-label design is acceptable.** For both dasatinib and nilotinib, CHMP accepted open-label designs because most of the endpoints are objectively measured[455](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=455)[457](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=457)[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=65) .
- **Missing-data rules matter.** In ENESTnd, a missing month-12 assessment counted as non-response unless MMR was present at both month 9 and month 15[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=56) . The key secondary endpoint was durable MMR, defined as MMR at both months 12 and 24 with no loss in between[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=57) .


The imatinib history shows how far expectations have moved. In early meetings for the first-line program, FDA said six-month CHR was not an adequate primary endpoint. It said superiority in MCyR at 24 months might support accelerated approval, and the parties ultimately agreed on superiority in time to progression[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=177)[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=178)[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=179) .


### Resistant or intolerant chronic-phase CML


Product / trial Design Primary endpoint Key result FDA pathway and endpoint view


Imatinib, Study 0110 (after interferon) Single-arm phase 2, n=532[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=92)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=174) MCyR (0 to 35% Ph+ metaphases); unconfirmed rate was the principal outcome[528](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=528)[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=531) 49.4% unconfirmed MCyR in the original analysis[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=531) Accelerated approval May 10, 2001. FDA considered MCyR in any setting, and CHR, reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit[940](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=940)[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=166)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=170)


Dasatinib, CA180013 / CA180017 / CA180034 Single-arm; randomized 2:1 vs high-dose imatinib (MCyR at 12 weeks); randomized 2x2 dose/schedule study[416](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=416)[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=283)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=285) MCyR[278](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=278)[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=283)[286](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=286) CP MCyR 45% in the single-arm studies; once-daily vs twice-daily difference 1.9% (95% CI −6.8% to 10.6%)[278](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=278)[286](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=286) Accelerated approval in 2006 with 24-month follow-up commitments; FDA described durable MCyR as a basis for accelerated approval[899](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=899)[900](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=900)[648](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=648)[649](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=649)


Nilotinib, A2101 Single-arm, open-label; CP and AP cohorts[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=124)[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=132) MCyR in CP[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=133)[503](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=503) 51% (95% CI 46% to 57%)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=133) Accelerated approval October 29, 2007, with 24-month follow-up required. FDA accepted bone-marrow cytogenetics, not FISH, as the validated measure[724](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=724)[732](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=732)[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=505)


Bosutinib, Study 200 Single-arm, open-label[630](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=630) MCyR by week 24[631](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=631)[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=570) 40.1% (imatinib only); 25.9% (imatinib plus at least one more TKI)[632](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=632)[631](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=631) Regular approval recommended. The team leader noted that FDA had previously accepted MCyR with 24 months of follow-up as evidence of clinical benefit in second-line CML[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=570)[572](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=572)


Ponatinib, PACE Single-arm, open-label, cohorts by phase and T315I status[382](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=382)[383](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=383) MCyR by 12 months (CP)[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=384) 55% overall; 70% in the T315I cohort[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=385)[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=386) Accelerated approval December 14, 2012, with a 24-month PMR; regular approval November 28, 2016[884](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=884)[885](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=885)[886](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=886)[887](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=887)[888](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=888)


Omacetaxine Combined analysis of two open-label, single-arm trials after at least two TKIs[311](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=311)[704](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=704) MCyR (CP); MaHR and/or MCyR (AP)[312](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=312)[702](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=702) CP MCyR 18.4%[313](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=313) Accelerated approval; the reviewer cited the lack of the 24 months of follow-up FDA expected for regular approval[706](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=706)


Asciminib, ASCEMBL Randomized 2:1, open-label phase 3 vs bosutinib, after at least two TKIs[344](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=344)[345](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=345)[602](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=602) MMR at week 24[346](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=346) 25.5% vs 13.2% (p=0.029)[338](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=338) Accelerated approval October 29, 2021; converted on October 12, 2022 after 96-week follow-up[965](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=965)[966](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=966)[967](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=967)[480](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=480)


ASCEMBL marks the change from MCyR to MMR in previously treated disease. During design review, FDA said MMR at 24 weeks "may be acceptable" as an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. It recommended MMR at two years as the first key secondary endpoint to verify that benefit[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=474)[475](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=475) . CHMP accepted MMR as a CML surrogate in principle but said week-24 MMR needed longer-term data, such as week-96 MMR, to support it[350](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=350) . CHMP also raised concerns about bosutinib discontinuations and how robust the result was under different missing-data assumptions[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=351) .


#### T315I-mutated disease


FDA recommended regular approval for asciminib in T315I-mutated CP-CML. The evidence came from a non-randomized, open-label cohort with 96-week MMR data[481](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=481)[482](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=482) . That study's primary endpoint was dose-limiting toxicity, and MMR was a secondary endpoint[483](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=483) . MMR by 24 weeks was 42% (19/45) and by 96 weeks 49%[608](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=608) . CHMP called this an uncontrolled exploratory study with substantial uncertainties. It said a randomized comparison with ponatinib would have been more appropriate[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=358)[361](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=361) .


### Accelerated- and blast-phase CML


In advanced-phase disease the primary endpoint has stayed hematologic:


- **Imatinib:** confirmed hematologic response (CHR, NEL or return to chronic phase) in single-arm phase 2 studies; FDA granted accelerated approval on hematologic-response surrogates[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=98)[99](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=99)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=170)[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=171) .
- **Dasatinib:** MaHR (CHR plus NEL, confirmed after four weeks). FDA called MaHR "reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit" and considered overall hematologic response less clinically significant[279](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=279)[653](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=653)[654](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=654) .
- **Nilotinib:** the protocol used overall hematologic response. FDA accepted CHR plus NEL but not return to chronic phase, and recommended assessing the endpoint without that component[506](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=506)[507](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=507) .
- **Ponatinib (PACE):** MaHR by 6 months, 57% in AP-CML and 31% in BP-CML[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=388) .
- **Bosutinib (Study 200):** confirmed CHR and overall hematologic response by week 48 were the stated efficacy endpoints[631](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=631)[634](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=634) .


### Pediatric CML


Pediatric programs have been single-arm and have used a range of endpoints:


- **Nilotinib (A2203):** single-arm phase 2. The primary endpoint was MMR at cycle 6 in resistant/intolerant patients. In newly diagnosed patients the co-primary endpoints were MMR by cycle 12 and CCyR at cycle 12[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=25)[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=59) .
- **Dasatinib:** EMA's assessment describes on-study MCyR as the primary endpoint for the imatinib-resistant/intolerant cohort and on-study CCyR for the newly diagnosed cohort[449](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=449)[451](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=451) .
- **Ponatinib (pediatric phase 2):** best MCyR within 12 months; 9/10 responded[214](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=214)[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=215) .
- **Bosutinib (BCHILD):** the primary endpoints were safety and pharmacokinetics. FDA used MCyR, MMR and response duration as descriptive efficacy measures to support regular approval[579](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=579)[580](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=580) . EMA likewise described the efficacy assessment as exploratory[245](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=245)[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=246) .


### Dose-optimization trials


The ponatinib OPTIC trial (NCT02467270) used a molecular threshold other than MMR. Its primary endpoint was BCR::ABL1 ≤1% IS at 12 months in patients with more than 1% at entry. In the 45 mg starting-dose group (reduced to 15 mg once the threshold was reached), 44% of patients achieved it[849](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=849)[852](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=852)[853](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=853) . OPTIC results are in the CP-CML labeling, and FDA records refer to a five-year OPTIC follow-up requirement[855](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=855)[889](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=889) .


### Design patterns across approvals


1. **Accelerated approval followed by conversion is the norm at FDA.** Imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib (first-line), ponatinib and asciminib (third-line and first-line) all received accelerated approval first[940](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=940)[944](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=944)[908](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=908)[725](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=725)[866](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=866)[884](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=884)[965](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=965)[970](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=970) . Conversion required 24-month follow-up in resistant/intolerant settings and 60-month follow-up for first-line indications[886](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=886)[900](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=900)[909](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=909)[735](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=735)[870](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=870) .
2. **First-line indications require randomized active-controlled superiority trials.** In the post-imatinib first-line approvals (dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, asciminib), the investigational TKI was compared with imatinib or a TKI chosen by the investigator[273](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=273)[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=126)[626](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=626)[597](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=597) . Imatinib itself was compared with interferon-alfa plus cytarabine.
3. **Later-line and advanced-phase indications accept single-arm trials.** FDA's nilotinib reviewers accepted no comparator because no effective control therapy existed[508](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=508)[509](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=509) . In the ponatinib review, FDA said a single-arm trial could support accelerated approval if responses were meaningful, durable and verifiable[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=15) . CHMP warned that a non-comparative design might not be acceptable for some resistant patients without a BCR-ABL mutation[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=197) .
4. **Assay quality affects whether a molecular endpoint can be reviewed.** In PACE, FDA could not adequately evaluate MMR as a secondary endpoint because assay-performance data had not been submitted[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=18) .
5. **Timepoints vary by agency and version.** FDA has accepted MMR at 12 months, 48 weeks and 24 weeks as primary endpoints, with longer follow-up confirming durability. EMA's current appendix recommends 18 months for superiority, and CHMP raised this point when it reviewed bosutinib's 12-month endpoint[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=128)[598](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=598)[346](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=346)[760](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=760)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cml-approval-endpoints-what-fda-and-ema?showSourceNumber=243) .
